subjects.description: A robotic-assisted surgical instrument, specifically a needle driver with metallic jaws and an articulated wrist joint, featuring a red 'S' logo.
subjects.appearance_details: Silver metallic finish, articulated joint, red circular logo with a white 'S'
subjects.relationship: Operates on the left side of the workspace, driving a needle through tissue.
subjects.pose: Articulated at the wrist, jaws gripping a curved needle
subjects.action: Executes a rotational motion to drive a needle through a tissue flap.
subjects.state_changes: Initial positioning followed by a clockwise rotation to puncture tissue.

subjects.description: A second surgical needle driver instrument, visible only by its tip and jaws.
subjects.relationship: Operates on the right side, holding the suture thread to maintain tension.
subjects.action: Holds suture thread steady during the needle driving process.
subjects.state_changes: Remains relatively static while maintaining tension on the suture.

actions.description: The left needle driver positions the needle against the underside of a tissue flap while the right driver holds the suture thread.
The left needle driver rotates, puncturing the needle through the tissue and beginning to pull it through.

segments.description: A single continuous take of a surgical suturing step where a needle is driven through tissue.
segments.key_changes: The primary change is the rotation and penetration of the needle through the tissue.

caption_json.temporal_caption: Beginning with a close-up laparoscopic view, the operative field shows moist, red tissue and two surgical instruments. A metallic left needle driver, marked with a red 'S' logo, holds a curved needle. Simultaneously, a right needle driver holds a dark suture thread taut. Starting at approximately two seconds, the left instrument performs a controlled clockwise rotation, pushing the needle tip through the edge of a tissue flap from beneath. The needle emerges on the upper surface of the tissue. Throughout this action, the right instrument maintains its grip on the suture thread, keeping it clear of the needle's path. The static camera captures the precise movement under bright, reflective surgical lighting until the needle has fully penetrated the tissue layer.
